Messages.Author: Murphy Christopher J
Messages.Body:
When a torpored Tremere "leaves torpor during your Master phase", does it
just happen (like a Master effect)? Or is it an actual event with some
associated Stealth value (which could be blocked)?
I thought it was the former for 8 months until today.

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <3m1cf5$2...@knot.queensu.ca>, 3cj...@qlink.queensu.ca (Murphy
Christopher J) wrote:



And for 8 months you were correct. A Tremere leaves torpor during it's
Meth's master phase if that Meth own the Chantry. There is no stealth,
there is no chance of blocking. It is a master phase effect.
A question still arises as to whether it is required. For example, blood
must come off another Tremere or from the pool. If you have 3 pool left,
and your only 3 tremere are in torpor, and you have the Chantry, do you
_have_ to pay the 3 pool to bring your vamps out of torpor, thereby outing
yourself in the Master phase, or is bringing out a vamp optional?

My group has always played it as an optional effect. But I believe the
wording on the card supports a mandatory interpretation. What does
everyone else think?

stephen

My group considers the use of the Chantry mandatory. However, Chantry reads
"A Tremere leaves torpor during your master phase ... " I interpret that
to mean ONE tremere in torpor, not ALL tremeres in torpor.

Besides, if 3 of your vampires are in torpor and you have only 3 blood left
in your pool, you're in serious trouble anyway.

Pat

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3mbtld$e...@redwood.cs.scarolina.edu>,

L. Scott Johnson <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> wrote:
>>>:> Mandatory. The card is phrased that way. It fits in with the extremely
>>>:> close nature of the Tremere clan too.
>>>

>>>You of course realize that this means the Talbot's Chainsaw's attack is also
>>>mandatory.
>

>> How? TC is equipment, Chantry is a master card. They don't
>>relate.
>
>Because both say "Something happens"
>If one means that it is mandatory, so does the other.

But both are completely different cards, defined completely
separately. You're trying to compare apples and oranges. You can't say
"because they're both round they both tase good." The characteristics
of a master card are completely different from those of a minion card,
and comparing a superficial characteristic of the cards is like making
the comparison above.

Finally, for whatever value you place on these things, in the
DTR for 12/22/94, question 17 was "Is using the Chantry optional?"
Answer: Yes. And we've all seen Tom's ruling that equipment is
optional.
It happens to match that both were ruled the same way, anyway.
Optional. But if they were different, I'd still stick to my guns...


